body:
That’s a new feature of Fastify v2. We decided not to backport it, because it could change the behavior of users.

V2 is going out soon, the likely solution is to upgrade.
@mcollina I've made some investigation. It appears that code above works fine in fastify `1.13.4`. So it seems that it was broken in `1.14`.
cc @Eomm can you take a look? This is likely caused by one of your latest changes.
One more clarification: version 1.14.0 already has this bug, so bug is hiding somewhere between 1.13.4 and 1.14.0 releases.

@Eomm there are several cases. One of them - adding global schemes that will be used in all routes, services, etc., so `whereAddTheSchema` should be "root" fastify instance or as you call it app instance.

Real world use-case is a plugin that adds possible error schemes for different error codes, that later could be used in response schema just like `error404#`. Or, for example, a plugin that exports a function or number of functions that takes some object as an item schema and generates proper filter, update schemes.

Understood, I'm checking how it could be solved.

Only as memo, the change comes from this PR https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/1370

Just as a workaround probably `addSchema` could generate some hash of schema object and compare it with existing schema or use `deepEqual` to skip adding duplicate schemas. But I think there should be more elegant solution.
@Eomm one option could be to revert #1370 in v1. In fact, it was a breaking change.

issue.title: fix: don't add twice a json schema to an encapsulated object in tree
